message.content:
I need to fetch all pull requests created in December 2024 (2024-12-01 to 2024-12-31) from the cli/cli GitHub repository using the GitHub Search API (unauthenticated). 

The GitHub Search API endpoint is: https://api.github.com/search/issues

Use the query: `repo:cli/cli is:pr created:2024-12-01..2024-12-31`

The search API returns max 100 results per page. First, fetch page 1 with per_page=100 to get the total_count. If total_count > 100, fetch subsequent pages too.

Save each page response to /tmp/prs_page_N.json

Then, once all pages are fetched, I need to get the detailed PR info (specifically merge info) for each PR. The search API doesn't give mergedAt. So for each PR number, fetch:
  https://api.github.com/repos/cli/cli/pulls/{number}

This gives merged_at, created_at, state, merged, user.login, etc.

Save all the detailed PR data into a single JSON array at /tmp/prs_detailed.json

Use curl with -s flag. Add header "Accept: application/vnd.github+json". 
Be mindful of rate limits (60/hour unauthenticated). If there are too many PRs, we may need to batch.

Start by fetching page 1 to see total_count, then plan accordingly.

content.text: I'll start by fetching page 1 to see the total count of PRs.

input.command: curl -s -H "Accept: application/vnd.github+json" "https://api.github.com/search/issues?q=repo:cli/cli+is:pr+created:2024-12-01..2024-12-31&per_page=100&page=1" -o /tmp/prs_page_1.json && python3 -c "import json; d=json.load(open('/tmp/prs_page_1.json')); print('total_count:', d.get('total_count')); print('items_on_page:', len(d.get('items',[]))); print('incomplete_results:', d.get('incomplete_results'))"
input.description: Fetch page 1 of PR search results and display total count

content.text: 50 PRs to fetch. The unauthenticated rate limit is 60 requests/hour. We've used 1 request for the search, so we have 59 left -- enough for all 50 detail requests. Let me fetch them in batches with a small delay to be respectful of rate limits.

input.command:
python3 << 'PYEOF'
import json, subprocess, time, sys

# Load PR numbers
d = json.load(open('/tmp/prs_page_1.json'))
numbers = [item['number'] for item in d['items']]

detailed = []
total = len(numbers)

for i, pr_num in enumerate(numbers):
    url = f"https://api.github.com/repos/cli/cli/pulls/{pr_num}"
    result = subprocess.run(
        ["curl", "-s", "-H", "Accept: application/vnd.github+json", url],
        capture_output=True, text=True
    )
    try:
        pr_data = json.loads(result.stdout)
        if 'message' in pr_data and 'rate limit' in pr_data.get('message', '').lower():
            print(f"Rate limited at PR #{pr_num} (index {i}). Stopping.")
            # Save what we have so far
            break
        detailed.append(pr_data)
        print(f"[{i+1}/{total}] PR #{pr_num} - state:{pr_data.get('state')} merged:{pr_data.get('merged')} merged_at:{pr_data.get('merged_at')}")
    except json.JSONDecodeError:
        print(f"[{i+1}/{total}] PR #{pr_num} - FAILED to parse response")
    
    # Small delay to be respectful (1.2s between requests)
    if i < total - 1:
        time.sleep(1.2)

# Save all detailed data
with open('/tmp/prs_detailed.json', 'w') as f:
    json.dump(detailed, f, indent=2)

print(f"\nDone. Saved {len(detailed)} detailed PR records to /tmp/prs_detailed.json")
PYEOF

python3 << 'PYEOF'
import json

data = json.load(open('/tmp/prs_detailed.json'))

merged = [pr for pr in data if pr.get('merged')]
not_merged = [pr for pr in data if not pr.get('merged')]
open_prs = [pr for pr in data if pr.get('state') == 'open']

print(f"=== Summary of cli/cli PRs created in December 2024 ===")
print(f"Total PRs:      {len(data)}")
print(f"Merged:         {len(merged)}")
print(f"Closed (unmerged): {len(not_merged)}")
print(f"Still open:     {len(open_prs)}")
print()

# Unique authors
authors = set(pr['user']['login'] for pr in data)
print(f"Unique authors: {len(authors)}")
print(f"Authors: {', '.join(sorted(authors))}")
print()

print("--- Merged PRs ---")
for pr in sorted(merged, key=lambda x: x['merged_at']):
    print(f"  #{pr['number']:>5}  merged {pr['merged_at'][:10]}  by {pr['user']['login']:<20}  {pr['title'][:70]}")

print()
print("--- Closed (not merged) PRs ---")
for pr in sorted(not_merged, key=lambda x: x['number']):
    print(f"  #{pr['number']:>5}  by {pr['user']['login']:<20}  {pr['title'][:70]}")
PYEOF
